title: feat(spec,lint,cli): a screen field's option labels and a flow's terminal toasts have keys in the flows translation face
body:
Part of #22507
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

This PR keys two of the three user-read flow slots that had no key in the `flows` translation face: a screen field's option labels and the flow's terminal toasts. It also adds the family pin. The third slot, a screen's `description`, is server-rendered, so this PR stops there and reports it for a decision (see "Where this PR stops"). That is why the first line is `Part of` rather than the closing keyword the dispatch named: merging this must leave the card open for the `description` half.

## What changes

**`@objectstack/spec`**

- `TranslationDataSchema.flows` gains three keys.
  - `flows.FLOW.successMessage` and `flows.FLOW.errorMessage`: the terminal toasts. Aliases `success` / `successText` / `error` / `errorText` rename onto them.
  - `flows.FLOW.screens.NODE_ID.fields.FIELD.options.VALUE`: a screen field's option labels. `choices` / `values` rename onto `options`.
- Each option is keyed by its value coerced to a string, `String(value)`, through one function: `flowScreenFieldOptionKey` (`@objectstack/spec/automation`). This is the seat's choice in the claim. It is also the console select's own key for an option (`SelectItem value={String(o.value)}` in objectui's `ScreenView`), and the coercion `translateAction` already applies to an action param's inline options.
- **The one narrowing.** `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` refuses two options of one field whose values collide as text, such as `1` and `"1"`, `true` and `"true"`, or a repeated value.
  - The refusal lands at the second option's `value`. At the flow door it reads `nodes[1].config.fields[0].options[1].value`.
  - It leads with `SCREEN_FIELD_OPTION_VALUE_COLLISION`, names both options by position and value, and gives the remedy.
  - Measured reach: 0 collisions. The examples hold 35 flows, 6 screens, 2 option fields and 10 options, all with string values (measured at `37c711449` by loading the `app-crm`, `app-todo` and `app-showcase` flows). hotcrm at `f0afcbda0` and hotclm at `14c899fc4` were read by inspection: their option values are string literals or come from an object field's string options.
- `translateFlow` applies the toasts, only where the flow authors one, so a bundle cannot add a toast. It also applies the option labels, option by option, falling back to the authored label.
  - `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions(bundle, flowName, nodeId, field, opts)` is new, for a runner that holds a served `ScreenFieldSpec`.
  - `FLOW_TERMINAL_MESSAGE_KEYS` is new, the key list the extractor and the schema pin share.
- The exclusion texts that no longer hold were rewritten: `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_NO_OPTIONS` is removed, the toast guidance is removed, and the `description` guidance now says why it is unkeyed and what the screen face carries.
- The liveness ledger gains `translation/flows.successMessage` and `flows.errorMessage`, both `planned` (contract-first split, as `screens` was), and dated notes on `flows` and `flows.screens` for the option map.

**`@objectstack/lint`**: `validateTranslationReferences` judges both new key families.

- A translated toast over a flow that declares none is `translation-target-unknown` (error).
- An option key that names no declared option, or names one by its label, is `translation-option-key-unknown` (warning). This is the same rule and severity as the object-field and action-param legs.

**`@objectstack/cli`**: `os i18n extract` and the coverage gate scaffold and demand the new keys in the `flow` bucket.

- The option keys go through the same key function.
- The completion toast is demanded for a flow with a screen, and the failure toast for every flow. Each predicate mirrors the reader that will draw it (see below).

**Examples**: `app-crm` (zh-CN toasts) and `app-todo` (zh-CN and ja-JP option labels) are translated, so `check:i18n-coverage` holds at its baseline. Without this it grew 101 → 103 and 106 → 126. These files are outside the claim's file surface; the report declares it.

## The enumeration, and the family pin

`packages/spec/src/system/flows-translation-face.test.ts` walks the flow schemas mechanically and lists every text-bearing leaf. Each leaf is held against one recorded disposition: `keyed` (a face key that must parse and survive), `noReader`, `elsewhere` (another declared route, which must exist) or `owed` (pinned exactly, shrink-only).

- **Tier 1** covers every text leaf of `FlowSchema` (minus `nodes`), `FlowNodeSchema` (minus `config`), `ScreenConfigSchema` and `EndConfigSchema`.
- **Tier 2** covers the copy-named text leaves of every other declared node contract (the builtin executor contracts and `approval`), plus every `FLOW_NODE_TEXT_SLOTS` entry.

It also fails on a stale row, and on a face key that no slot fills.

| Slot | Disposition |
|---|---|
| `Flow.label` | keyed `label` |
| `Flow.successMessage` / `errorMessage` | keyed (new) |
| screen `title`, and a screen node's `label` as its fallback heading | keyed `screens.NODE_ID.title` |
| screen field `label` / `placeholder` / `inlineHelpText` | keyed |
| screen field `options[].label` | keyed `…options.VALUE` (new) |
| end `message` (refused) | keyed `refusals.NODE_ID.message` |
| **screen `description`** | **owed: server-rendered, decision pending** |
| notify `title` / `message` | elsewhere: the notify `template` path (sys_email_template, per recipient locale) |
| **approval `decisionOutputs[].label`** | **owed: read in the approval decision dialog, no face at all** |
| `Flow.description`, edge `label`, variables, ids, predicates, `defaultValue`, `defaults`, `objectName`, framework/lock fields, … | noReader, each with its reason |

`noReader` means that no person running the flow reads the text. `Flow.description` is drawn by Studio's metadata viewer only, so it is recorded that way, with that reason.

**It bites** (ablation, each leg through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` with an anchor hit of 1 → 0, the pin run under the verify lock, then restored with blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`). Predicted: red. Observed: red.

- Planting `subtitle: z.string().optional()` on `ScreenConfigSchema` (blob `5b4cf3fe` → `ac16dd5a` → `5b4cf3fe`) gives 1 failed / 6 passed: `expected [ 'screen.subtitle' ] to deeply equal []`.
- Renaming the face's `successMessage` key (blob `8d5dd093` → `05480fb1` → `8d5dd093`) gives 2 failed / 5 passed: the keyed-row check and the face-fill check.

## Where this PR stops: a screen's `description` is server-rendered

The dispatch orders a stop before touching `service-automation` if a slot proves server-rendered, and `description` does. `service-automation`'s screen executor renders `config.description` per run through `renderTextSlot` (`{{ }}` holes over the flow's variables) and serves the result as `ScreenSpec.description`.

An overlay on the served string would draw a translated hole literally. The face's existing `title` key already has that boundary, as FlowRunner's own header records. Templated descriptions are real: app-todo's `success_screen` (`Task "{{ subject }}" created successfully!`) and hotclm's `contract_intake` "First version" screen (`description: '{templateNote}'`).

So the key is not added. The options for the seat:

- **A.** The engine picks the translated template in the run's locale before `renderTextSlot`, the `refusals` route. This touches `service-automation`, and the same change should move `title` too.
- **B.** A client overlay, with the schema refusing a `{{ }}` hole in a translated `description`. A templated description then stays untranslatable.
- **C.** A client overlay with `title`'s silent boundary.

The pin records `description` as owed, so whichever lands must delete that row.

## What the objectui runner must read (for the seat's objectui card)

- `flows.FLOW.screens.NODE_ID.fields.FIELD.options.VALUE`: in `FlowRunner.tsx` `localizeScreen`, set each field's `options` to `resolveFlowScreenFieldOptions(bundle, flowName, screen.nodeId, field, { locale: language })` before `ScreenView` draws its `SelectItem`s.
  - Not through `FLOW_SCREEN_FIELD_COPY_KEYS`: the option map is not a string key and is deliberately not in that list.
- `flows.FLOW.successMessage`: in `FlowRunner.tsx`, the terminal-success toast (`outcome.successMessage || t('flowRunner.completed', …)`), via `translateFlow({ name: flowName, successMessage: outcome.successMessage }, bundle, { locale: language }).successMessage`.
- `flows.FLOW.errorMessage`: in `utils/flowResponse.ts` `flowFailureMessage`, which reads `data.errorMessage`, from `error.details.errorMessage` on the 400 `FLOW_FAILED` path. It is read by FlowRunner's resume and by both launch hosts through `judgeFlowLaunch` (`useConsoleActionRuntime`, `RecordDetailView`).
  - The launch path has no bundle or flow name there today, so the card threads them.
- The runner's header notes that say `description` / `inlineHelpText` / `FlowSchema.successMessage` are off the surface are stale.
- ⛔ No runner-side guessing from an object field's options: a screen field declares no such binding.

## Verification (final head `c17df03f0`, which merges `origin/main` `4638625e0`)

- **Typecheck**: `pnpm --filter PKG run typecheck` exited 0 for `@objectstack/spec` (source, scripts, and the test layer: 52 files / 246 errors / 135 pinned signatures held), `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/cli`.
- **Spec tiers in full**, under the verify lock:
  - `local`: 637 files, 18977 passed and 1 todo.
  - `repo`: 54 files, 915 passed.
- **Lint**: the full suite, 133 files / 6096 passed. `validate-translation-references.test.ts` alone: 162 passed.
- **CLI**: the unit-tier `test/i18n-*` files, 24 files / 285 passed. The new `i18n-flow-toast-option-coverage.test.ts` is among them. The integration tier is declared to CI.
- **Generated**: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` reports "All 15 generated artifacts are up to date", measured against a dist built by that run after the merge. The dropped-refinements count is unchanged at 688 / 226: the collision check lives in the existing `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` refinement.
- **Gates**: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 115 commands at this head. All 115 were run with their exit codes recorded, and `--ran` reports "115 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero)".
  - 114 exited 0.
  - `check:skill-examples` and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` first refused (exit 3, PREREQUISITE NOT MET). They exited 0 after building the named packages.
  - `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exits 1, and it is not this diff. It reads `ABSENT SYMBOL … attachment-access-hooks.ts#canEdit` and `SYMBOL ANCHORS LOST — 27 … floor is 28` in `areas/attachments-storage.json`. A clean worktree of `origin/main` `4638625e0` exits 1 with the same two lines. This diff touches neither file.
- **ESLint**, narrowed to the 17 changed `.ts` files: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` reports 17 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - None of the files is ignored; an ignored file would be a warning.
  - `eslint.config.mjs` enables no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file.
- **Size**: about 1,690 changed lines, generated files included.

## Acceptance notes

- The two new key families are `planned`. The objectui runner reads neither yet, so until its card lands a translated option or toast is stored and the authored text is drawn. Meanwhile the extractor demands them, the same contract-first window `screens` had.
- The screen `title` key has the same server-render boundary as `description` (a translated `{{ }}` hole draws literally). Option A above would fix both.
- Bulk-action params still exclude option labels with the old "value is unconstrained" reasoning (`BULK_PARAM_NO_OPTIONS`). An action param's inline options are keyed by `String(value)` with no collision refusal. Neither is in this card.
